target: docs/odp/10-ratio-to-another-part.md (equal to the culm) with docs/odp/09-relation-to-another-part.md (shorter than the culm), joined by docs/odp/07-alternatives.md
reason: A comparison of the leaf's length with a second part, the culm (stem PO_0009047), given as two alternatives. It is not a quality of the leaf alone.

target: new: compound of two values (erect PATO_0000622 + curved PATO_0000406)
reason: A hyphenated compound of two orientation values (erect, then arching). The previous review mapped arcuate to PATO_0000406 curved.

target: new: compound of two values (erose PATO_0001368 + scalloped PATO_0001889)
reason: A compound of two margin values, both already in PATO (crenulate is a synonym of scalloped). No new term is needed.
A loose comparison that is applied to unrelated parts (a fruit wing, a petal) and has no fixed botanical meaning. Its only possible mappings (bifurcated, praemorse) are guesses.
A misspelling of glabrescent (the second example is glabrescent with a soft hyphen in it). Both spellings should go to the existing FLOPO value class.
Made wider towards one end, as with the reviewed rule for 'expanded' (C181). 'Gradually' is a degree word and is kept in the record.
Same meaning as the reviewed rule for 'narrowed' (C172): a base that narrows gradually is tapered.
A ligule truncate at an incline: it ends in a straight edge that is oblique to its long axis. This is exactly the existing FLOPO value class.
Jar-like means swollen below and contracted at the mouth, which is how FLOPO defines urceolate (urn- or pitcher-shaped).
A ladle is a deep spoon, so a ladle-like bract is a concave blade shaped like a spoon. PATO's spoon-shaped is a concave 3-D shape.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum between two values: light brown to greyish brown)
reason: A colour range between two values, not a single quality. It belongs to the continuum pattern, with each end grounded as a colour.

'Midveined' or 'with midvein' says that a midvein is present, like the reviewed rules for veined and nerved. For bracts and bracteoles, check that ELK accepts PO_0020139 as part of a phyllome; if not, use vascular bundle (PO_0005020). 'Distinctly' and 'faintly' go to conspicuous or inconspicuous.
A vein that forks several times is branched. Bifurcated (PATO_0001784) covers a single fork only.
A pedicel bearing a node, especially at its apex, is the articulated (jointed) pedicel of floras. PO's node classes are stem nodes and don't fit a pedicel.

Authors use the word inconsistently: some mean 'inversely spatulate' (broadest at the base), others simply spatulate, and the examples don't show which. Only 3 statements, so a term would be doubtful.

target: new: compound of two values (papillose FLOPO:0991059 + pubescent hair PATO_0001320)
reason: A compound of two existing surface values: covered with short hairs and with papillae, or with papilla-like hairs. Both are already terms.

target: new: hair form and indumentum (trichome PO_0000282 pectinate FLOPO:0991033, as part of the organ; organ hispid PATO_0002339)
reason: 'Pectinate' describes how the stiff hairs are arranged (like comb teeth), not the shape of the leaf or lemma. Grounding it on the organ would be a wrong reading, as the valid-combination review found for 'stellate'.

target: new: compound of two values (peltate FLOPO:0991107 + auriculate PATO_0001981)
reason: A base with auricles that are attached inside the margin: a compound of two existing values, not a new quality.
A flat, roundish gland or disk is plate-like. PATO lists plate-like as an EXACT synonym of platelike.
'Roots proplike' names a kind of root (prop or brace root), not a quality of an ordinary root.
Pubigerous means bearing a pubescence (covered with short soft hairs), which is PATO_0001320. It is not PATO_0000455 pubescent, which is a maturity quality.

target: new: compound of two values (raceme-like FLOPO:0991197 + spike-like FLOPO:0991142)
reason: An inflorescence between a raceme and a spike (flowers subsessile on a simple axis). It is a compound of two existing FLOPO values.

target: docs/odp/00-part-and-quality.md (bearer lenticel PO_0000031 as part of the branch, with a round shape quality)
reason: A part with a quality, not a quality word. Lenticel presence is covered by the reviewed rule for 'lenticellate'; 'rounded', 'small' and 'dispersed' describe the lenticels.
'Without a septum' says that a fruit septum is absent (pattern 15).
PATO's discoid is a cylinder whose height is less than its diameter. 'Shallowly' only stresses the low height and can stay as a degree word in the record.
No standard botanical meaning. The examples (inner filaments, stamens) probably mean a filament widened at the base into shoulders, but the word alone doesn't say which shape.
Looks like a translation compound of 'slightly sinuate' and 'nicked' with no fixed meaning. 'Nicked' is not a defined margin term.
A loose comparison used for unrelated structures (cycad megasporophylls, sepals). It doesn't reliably mean spatulate or any other defined shape.

target: new: hair form and indumentum (trichome PO_0000282 star shaped PATO_0002065, as part of the organ; organ hispid PATO_0002339)
reason: 'Stellate' describes the hairs, and the reviewed pair and valid-combination tables block star shaped on the organ itself. If this pattern is not built, the alternative is a FLOPO class 'stellate-hairy' beside stellate-lepidote (FLOPO:0991304).

target: new: hair form and indumentum (trichome PO_0000282 star shaped PATO_0002065, as part of the organ; organ lanate PATO_0104357)
reason: Same structure as 'stellate hispid': woolly indumentum made of star-shaped hairs. The hair form belongs to the trichomes and the woolliness to the organ.
